claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys produced by standard synthesis routes typically contain no secondary nanoprecipitates.
The proposed intervention adds 1–3 wt% Ti to the refractory HEA.
Thermal aging after Ti addition will induce in situ formation of nanoscale TiC precipitates.
The intervention will produce a uniform dispersion of coherent nanoscale TiC precipitates in the refractory HEA matrix.
Nanoscale TiC precipitates impede dislocation motion through precipitation strengthening.
Nanoscale TiC precipitates can act as defect sinks under irradiation.
The TiC dispersion will increase yield strength relative to a refractory HEA without intentional nanoprecipitates.
The TiC dispersion will improve creep resistance relative to a refractory HEA without intentional nanoprecipitates.
The modified alloy will maintain thermal stability comparable to that of the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will maintain irradiation stability comparable to that of the baseline alloy.
The beneficial effects will persist during high-temperature exposure and irradiation representative of service conditions.
Variations in precipitate size, distribution, and coherency will affect the magnitude of the mechanical improvement.
